question.text: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of Standard Finance theory?

answer.text: Investors are rational and self-interested utility maximizers
Investors update their beliefs when they receive new information
Investors are guided by psychological biases in their decision making
Investors have access to all available information

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series X-B workbook (page 394), Standard Finance assumes investors are rational, risk averse, self-interested utility maximizers who update beliefs as new information arrives and have access to all available information. Page 395 contrasts this with Behavioural Finance, which places psychology at the core and treats biases as drivers of investment decisions. The Trap: "Update beliefs with new information" may sound behavioural, but page 394 lists it as a Standard Finance assumption: rational agents revise beliefs efficiently as new information comes in. Note: Map each option back to the page 394 list of Standard Finance assumptions; if it appears there, it is not the exception.
